result: With common caller-owned Episode setup/teardown and the same raw protocol callbacks, two endpoint Tasks have higher point latency than one Task driving both endpoints in both fixed orders. This is a finite combined execution-policy control, not a replacement peer ranking or a pure context-switch measurement.

scope.trace: Only4 streams x256KiB request and response, reverse completion in each pair, original connection-window holdout
preformal: One gdb reproduction reached the same uninitialized idle RawHarness state.
After the exact startup-order fix, one complete diagnostic episode per driver passed.
Formal counter-free executable also ran one complete warmup per arm per process.

common_responsibilities: Same caller-owned Episode contains two RawEndpoint, two RawWire and two adopted TcpStream owners; session initialization on caller in client/server order.
Same socketpair options, nghttp2 callbacks/options/settings, headers, per-stream body buffers and complete byte oracle; reverse pair responses and separate stream/connection flow acknowledgments.
Two RawWire each contain64KiB pending+64KiB input, zero-initialized by the same Episode construction in both arms; source total256KiB.
Sessions and fd owners destroyed in the same common destructor after join; storage destructors and Task lifecycle included in timed episode.
Workload strings and persistent one-worker Scheduler/IoContext plus idle RawHarness thread live outside both timed arms.
deliberate_differences: One spawn_task+join with the original manual interleaving and poll fallback versus two endpoint spawn_task+join, endpoint-local progress cadence, adaptive yields, readiness-aware TcpStream async fallback and completion Event.
Both arms now pay common TcpStream adoption and a caller-owned Episode; the original manual peer had no Task and used a separate worker. This control cannot replace that peer.
The endpoint policy may issue different empty I/O operations and split wire chunks differently while preserving the same payload/protocol responsibility. These are part of the tested combined policy.
Observed smoke server-to-client wire counts differ by65B. Neither actual control-frame composition nor terminal pending queue contents were recorded.

diagnostic.wire_difference: TwoTasks transferred65 fewer server-to-client wire bytes in the diagnostic episode. Payload, headers and consume/ack callback responsibilities are retained; actual control-frame composition was not decoded. Do not claim identical wire work or pureTask cost.
limits: These counts are from one non-timed complete episode per driver, not the formal episodes.
Direct recv/send wrappers count only the raw immediate seams; internal TcpStream/kernel async attempts are not counted. Async results record bytes and entry counts separately.
Both final descriptor-closed checks happen after the common Episode destructor and only in diagnostic builds.
Terminal RawWire begin/end, nghttp2_session_want_write and queued frame types were not recorded. No claim which frames account for65B.

terminal_boundary.manual: Loop exits when client.completed==4, then checks both endpoint.completed==4 and failure flags; no final want_write/drain check.
terminal_boundary.endpoints: Client exits at completed==4 and signals Event. Server waits for Event after all response pairs submitted, lastfirstresponse.output_done and its RawWire empty; both completed==4 checked after joins.
terminal_boundary.common: Both destroy sessions and transport owners after successful joins. Both source exit conditions permit nghttp2 control frames to remain queued; whether any actually remained was not recorded.
terminal_boundary.credit: Both arms execute the same raw_consume_readable callback loop: every consumed body chunk checks bytes and calls consume_stream and consume_connection. Emitting all terminal queued credit frames is not an additional completion requirement in either original boundary.

failure.cause: RawHarness starts worker_ before workload_/pending_/complete_/stopping_ are initialized; new idle worker entered run_raw with invalid workload. Episode had not started.
failure.fix: Move only worker_ declaration after all state it reads. No driver, session, protocol or Episode semantics changed.

limitations: Only two fixed-order processes; no cross-process confidence interval, significance or general-equivalence claim.
The observed delta includes Task count, join, progress/readiness cadence and yield strategy. It is not isolated fcontext cost or generic scheduler overhead.
Do not subtract this delta from another round Hyle-versus-manual number to claim attribution of the previously observed16-17% residual.
No Hyle HTTP2 public route runs here, so this does not remeasure the helper-fixed Hyle route.
ClockResolution is nanobench sampled resolution metadata; actual epoch durations and cross-process variability are separate and all preserved.
Hardware performance counters were disabled; JSON zero cycle/instruction fields are not measurements.
